breakfast.name: Full English Breakfast
instructions: Fry bacon and sausages
Fry or scramble eggs
Grill tomato and mushrooms
Heat beans
Toast bread
Serve everything on one large plate
breakfast.description: The full English fry-up — a monumental breakfast.

breakfast.name: Porridge with Golden Syrup
instructions: Cook oats in milk with salt
Drizzle with golden syrup
breakfast.description: Creamy porridge with golden syrup — a British winter morning.

breakfast.name: Full English Breakfast
ingredients: Black pudding (blood sausage -- optional but traditional)
instructions: The Full English is the iconic British breakfast -- a plateful of everything
Each region has its variation: Full Scottish adds haggis, Full Welsh adds laverbread
The components: bacon, sausages, eggs, beans, toast, tomato, mushrooms
Black pudding: a blood sausage from the north of England -- divisive but traditional
Served at "greasy spoons" (working-class cafes) across Britain
Also called a "fry-up"
Traditionally a weekend breakfast -- too substantial for workday mornings
Brown sauce (HP Sauce) or ketchup on the side -- the condiment choice is fiercely debated
breakfast.description: The iconic British fry-up -- Full English, a plate of back bacon, sausages, eggs, baked beans, toast, grilled tomato, mushrooms, and optionally black pudding. A weekend tradition at greasy spoon cafes. Brown sauce vs ketchup: a fiercely debated condiment choice.

breakfast.name: Porridge (Scottish Oats)
ingredients: Rolled oats (or pinhead/steel-cut oats for traditional Scottish porridge)
Optional toppings: berries, cream, golden syrup
instructions: Porridge is the Scottish and broader British breakfast staple
Traditional Scottish porridge: pinhead oats cooked slowly with water and salt -- no sugar
The modern version uses rolled oats with milk and sweet toppings
Samuel Johnson's dictionary famously defined oats as food for horses in England and people in Scotland
Quick, warming, and nutritious -- a wet-weather breakfast
breakfast.description: British breakfast staple -- porridge, oats cooked with water or milk. Traditional Scottish: pinhead oats, water, and salt only. Samuel Johnson famously defined oats as food for horses in England and people in Scotland. Warming and nutritious.

lunch.name: Fish and Chips
instructions: Cut thick chips, double-fry
Make beer batter
Dip fish, fry until golden
Serve with mushy peas, vinegar, tartar sauce
lunch.description: The UK's defining dish — battered fish, thick chips, and malt vinegar.

lunch.name: Ploughman's Lunch
instructions: Arrange all items on board
Serve with butter and crusty bread
lunch.description: Classic cold pub lunch — cheese, pickle, and crusty bread.

lunch.name: Ploughman's Lunch
ingredients: Strong cheddar cheese (a good aged cheddar)
instructions: The Ploughman's Lunch is the British pub cold lunch
A board of cheese, pickle, bread, and accompaniments
Branston pickle: the essential British condiment -- a chunky, sweet-tangy relish of vegetables
The cheese must be a proper cheddar -- not mild
Originally marketed by the Milk Marketing Board in the 1960s to sell more cheese
Despite the manufactured origin, it has become a genuine tradition
Eaten with a pint of ale in a pub garden on a summer day
lunch.description: British pub cold lunch -- Ploughman's, a board of aged cheddar, Branston pickle (the essential chunky relish), crusty bread, pickled onions, and apple. Originally a 1960s Milk Marketing Board invention to sell cheese -- now a genuine tradition. Best with a pint in a pub garden.

lunch.name: Cornish Pasty
instructions: The Cornish pasty is the handheld meat pie from Cornwall
Historically a tin miner's lunch -- the thick crimped edge was the handle (held by dirty hands, then discarded)
The filling must be raw when assembled -- it cooks inside the pastry
Protected by EU PGI status: a genuine Cornish pasty must be made in Cornwall
The crimp must be on the side, not the top
Beef skirt (not mince) cut into small pieces -- this is crucial to authenticity
The swede (rutabaga) and potato provide moisture inside the sealed pastry
lunch.description: Cornwall's handheld meat pie -- Cornish pasty, shortcrust pastry crimped on the side around beef skirt, potato, swede, and onion. Historically a tin miner's lunch: the crimp was the handle for dirty hands. EU PGI protected. Filling goes in raw and cooks inside.

lunch.name: Scotch Egg
instructions: The Scotch egg is a boiled egg wrapped in sausage meat, breaded, and fried
Invented in London by Fortnum & Mason in 1738 (they claim)
Despite the name, it is not Scottish
Eaten cold at picnics or hot from the fryer
The yolk debate: slightly runny yolk or fully hard-boiled -- divides the nation
A pub snack, picnic food, and petrol station staple
lunch.description: British boiled egg wrapped in sausage meat -- Scotch egg, breaded and fried (or baked). Claimed by Fortnum & Mason (1738). Not actually Scottish. The yolk debate (runny vs hard) divides the nation. Pub snack, picnic food, petrol station staple.

dinner.name: Sunday Roast
instructions: Roast beef 2 hours
Roast potatoes in dripping
Make Yorkshire pudding batter, bake in hot fat
Make gravy from drippings
Serve together with horseradish
dinner.description: The British Sunday roast — beef, Yorkshires, roast potatoes, and gravy.

dinner.name: Shepherd's Pie
instructions: Brown lamb with onion, carrots, peas
Add tomato paste, Worcestershire, broth
Pour into dish, top with mashed potato
Sprinkle cheese
Bake at 200°C until golden
dinner.description: Lamb mince under golden mashed potato — the comfort classic.

dinner.name: Sunday Roast
ingredients: Roasting joint: beef (with Yorkshire pudding), lamb (with mint sauce), chicken, or pork (with apple sauce)
Roast potatoes (par-boiled then roasted in goose fat or oil until crispy)
Yorkshire pudding (batter: eggs, flour, milk -- baked in hot fat)
Vegetables: carrots, peas, green beans, cabbage
instructions: The Sunday Roast is the British weekly ritual -- the anchor of family life
A roasted joint of meat with all the trimmings
Yorkshire pudding: a crispy, risen batter pudding baked in hot fat -- NOT a dessert despite the name
Roast potatoes: the make-or-break element -- must be crispy outside, fluffy inside
Gravy: made from the meat pan drippings -- instant gravy is sacrilege
Each meat has its condiment: beef with horseradish, lamb with mint sauce, pork with apple sauce
Eaten after the pub on Sunday -- a tradition dating back centuries
The Sunday Roast is so important it was nominated as a UNESCO cultural heritage candidate
dinner.description: British weekly ritual -- the Sunday Roast, a roasted meat joint with crispy roast potatoes, Yorkshire pudding (not a dessert -- risen batter baked in hot fat), gravy from pan drippings, and vegetables. Each meat has its condiment: beef/horseradish, lamb/mint, pork/apple. The anchor of British family life.

dinner.name: Shepherd's Pie
ingredients: Lamb mince (shepherd's pie uses lamb; cottage pie uses beef)
Mashed potato topping (butter and milk, piped or forked on top)
instructions: Shepherd's pie is the British baked meat-and-potato pie -- a distinction matters:
Shepherd's pie = lamb (shepherds tend sheep)
Cottage pie = beef
Mixing them up is a British faux pas
Seasoned lamb mince with vegetables, topped with creamy mashed potato, baked until golden
Worcestershire sauce: the essential British flavoring -- fermented anchovy and vinegar
A comfort food -- warming, filling, and cheap to make
dinner.description: British baked meat pie -- Shepherd's pie (MUST be lamb; beef = cottage pie, and mixing them up is a faux pas). Seasoned lamb mince with vegetables topped with mashed potato and baked golden. Worcestershire sauce for depth. Warming comfort food.

dinner.name: Fish and Chips
ingredients: White fish: cod or haddock fillet
Beer batter: flour, beer, baking powder, salt
instructions: Fish and chips is the iconic British takeaway -- the national dish argument always includes it
The batter: beer batter gives a light, crispy coating
The chips: thick-cut, not thin fries -- soft inside, crispy edges
Mushy peas: a love-or-hate side -- marrowfat peas boiled into a bright green mush
Traditionally wrapped in newspaper (now illegal for food hygiene)
Malt vinegar and salt: the only proper seasoning
Chip shops (chippies) are found in every British town
Friday night fish and chips -- a British tradition linked to Catholic fish Fridays
dinner.description: Iconic British takeaway -- fish and chips, beer-battered cod or haddock with thick-cut chips, mushy peas, and malt vinegar. Traditionally newspaper-wrapped. Chippies in every town. Friday night fish and chips -- linked to Catholic fish Friday tradition.

snacks.name: Scotch Egg
instructions: Wrap eggs in sausage meat
Coat in flour, egg, breadcrumbs
Deep fry until golden
Serve with mustard
snacks.description: Hard-boiled egg wrapped in sausage meat, crumbed and fried.

snacks.name: Sausage Roll
ingredients: Pork sausage meat (seasoned with sage, pepper, nutmeg)
instructions: The sausage roll is the British pastry staple -- pork in puff pastry
Sausage meat wrapped in puff pastry and baked until golden and flaky
Greggs (the bakery chain) sells more sausage rolls than any other item
A football match, picnic, and Christmas party staple
The vegan sausage roll (Greggs launched it in 2019) became a cultural moment
snacks.description: British puff pastry classic -- sausage roll, seasoned pork in flaky puff pastry. Greggs sells more than any other item. Football match, picnic, and Christmas party staple. The vegan version (Greggs, 2019) became a cultural moment.

snacks.name: Cheese and Pickle Sandwich
instructions: The cheese and pickle sandwich is the most British sandwich that exists
Cheddar cheese and Branston pickle between two slices of buttered bread
Found in every supermarket meal deal across Britain
The "meal deal" (sandwich + drink + snack for a set price) is a British institution
Simple, satisfying, and deeply nostalgic
snacks.description: The most British sandwich -- cheese and pickle, strong cheddar with Branston pickle on buttered bread. Found in every supermarket meal deal. The meal deal (sandwich + drink + snack for a set price) is a British institution.

snacks.name: Crumpet
instructions: Crumpets are the British teatime bread -- spongy, holey, and toasted
A yeasted batter cooked on a griddle in metal rings
The bubbles rise through the batter creating the characteristic holes on top
Toasted until crispy on the outside, spongy inside
The holes: designed to absorb melted butter -- a delivery mechanism for butter
Eaten with butter alone, or with Marmite, honey, or jam
snacks.description: British teatime spongy bread -- crumpets, yeasted batter cooked in rings on a griddle. The holes on top absorb melted butter (they are a butter delivery mechanism). Toasted crispy outside, spongy inside. Eaten with butter, Marmite, honey, or jam.

desserts.name: Sticky Toffee Pudding
ingredients: Toffee sauce: butter, cream, brown sugar
instructions: Soak dates in hot water
Make sponge batter with dates
Bake at 175°C 35 min
Make toffee sauce
Pour sauce over warm pudding
Serve with ice cream
desserts.description: Dense date sponge drenched in toffee sauce.

desserts.name: Sticky Toffee Pudding
ingredients: Toffee sauce: butter, double cream, dark brown sugar
instructions: Sticky toffee pudding is the British dessert -- a moist date sponge drenched in toffee sauce
The dates are soaked in hot water with baking soda -- they dissolve into the batter
The result is a deeply moist, dark, and dense sponge cake
The toffee sauce: butter, cream, and dark brown sugar -- poured over generously
Served with custard, cream, or vanilla ice cream
Invented at the Sharrow Bay Hotel in the Lake District (1960s)
The pub dessert menu staple -- it appears on almost every pub menu in Britain
desserts.description: British pub dessert classic -- sticky toffee pudding, moist date sponge cake drenched in toffee sauce (butter, cream, brown sugar). Invented at Sharrow Bay Hotel, Lake District (1960s). Appears on almost every pub menu in Britain. Served with custard or ice cream.

desserts.name: Victoria Sponge
ingredients: Butter, caster sugar (equal weight to eggs)
instructions: The Victoria sponge is the classic British layer cake -- named after Queen Victoria
Two rounds of light sponge cake sandwiched with jam and cream
The all-in-one sponge method: butter and sugar creamed, eggs added, flour folded in
The top is simply dusted with icing sugar -- no frosting, no fuss
Queen Victoria reportedly took a slice with her afternoon tea
The benchmark of home baking -- judged at every village fete baking competition
The Great British Bake Off has made it a national obsession
desserts.description: Classic British layer cake -- Victoria sponge, named after Queen Victoria. Two light sponge rounds sandwiched with jam and cream, dusted with icing sugar. The benchmark of home baking, judged at every village fete. The Great British Bake Off made it a national obsession.

drinks.name: Proper Cup of Tea
instructions: Boil water, warm teapot
Add tea, pour boiling water
Steep 4 min
Add milk
Debate whether milk goes first
drinks.description: Strong tea with milk — the UK runs on this.

drinks.name: Pimm's Cup
instructions: Fill glass with ice
Add Pimm's and lemonade
Garnish with fruit, cucumber, and mint

drinks.name: Pimm's Cup
instructions: Pimm's is the quintessential British summer drink
Pimm's No. 1: a gin-based liqueur with herbs and spices -- the recipe is secret
Mixed with sparkling lemonade and served in a tall jug with fruit and cucumber
The drink of Wimbledon, Henley Regatta, and every garden party
British lemonade is carbonated (not still like American lemonade)
The cucumber is essential -- it provides the refreshing crispness
Drinking Pimm's means summer has arrived
drinks.description: Quintessential British summer drink -- Pimm's Cup, gin-based herbal liqueur mixed with sparkling lemonade, cucumber, strawberries, mint, and orange. The drink of Wimbledon, Henley Regatta, and every garden party. Cucumber is essential. Pimm's means summer has arrived.
